definition: In computer vision, articulated body pose estimation is the task of algorithmically determining the pose of a body composed of connected parts (joints and rigid parts) from image or video data.
details: This challenging problem, central to enabling robots and other systems to understand human actions and interactions, has been a long-standing research area due to the complexity of modeling the relationship between visual observations and pose, as well as the wide range of applications.

explainer.lead: Articulated body pose estimation teaches a computer to work out how a body’s connected parts are arranged in an image or video. It matters because robots and other systems need that information to understand human actions and interactions.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a person made from sticks joined together at the shoulders, elbows, and knees. This task is like looking at a photo and figuring out where all the sticks and joints are. A computer can then better understand what the person’s body is doing.
tiers.practitioner: A system takes image or video data as input and estimates the pose of a body represented by joints and rigid parts. It is used where software must interpret human actions or interactions. The central difficulty is reliably mapping visual observations to that pose.
tiers.paperLevel: Given image or video data I, estimate a pose P for an articulated body composed of connected joints and rigid parts. The problem is learning or computing the relationship between visual observations I and pose P. Its difficulty comes from the complexity of that relationship.

explainer.example: Given a video of a person waving, the system estimates the arrangement of the person’s joints and rigid body parts, including the raised arm, for each pose it analyzes.

usedIn.name: Human interaction systems
usedIn.detail: Supports systems that need to interpret people’s poses while interacting.

explainer.intuition: Think of the body as a collection of rigid pieces connected at joints. Pose estimation means determining how those pieces are arranged from what a camera sees.
howItWorks: Take an image or video containing a body.
Examine the visual observations of its connected parts.
Estimate the arrangement of the body’s joints and rigid parts.
Return that arrangement as the estimated body pose.
explainer.whyItMatters: Body pose gives machines a structured way to interpret human movement. That makes it an important step toward understanding actions and interactions.
misconceptions: It is not the same as action recognition: it estimates body pose, not the name of an action.
It concerns a body of connected parts, rather than treating the body as one rigid object.
